values.name: Client Value Creation
values.description: Enabling clients to become high-performance businesses and building long-term relationships by being responsive and delivering measurable value.

values.name: One Global Network
values.description: Leveraging the power of global insight, relationships, collaboration and learning to deliver exceptional service to clients.

values.name: Respect for the Individual
values.description: Valuing diversity, ensuring an interesting and inclusive environment, and treating people as they would like to be treated.

values.name: Best People
values.description: Attracting, developing and retaining the best talent, challenging people, and demonstrating a 'can-do' attitude.

values.name: Integrity
values.description: Being ethically unyielding and honest, and inspiring trust by saying what we mean and matching behaviours to words.

values.name: Stewardship
values.description: Fulfilling obligations to build a better, stronger and more durable company for future generations, with an owner mentality.

interview_expectations.description: Demonstrating Client Value Creation, One Global Network, Respect for the Individual, Best People, Integrity, and Stewardship.
Showcasing logical problem-solving, quantitative aptitude, and role-specific technical skills.
Displaying strong presentation abilities, cultural fit, and professional communication during HR rounds.
Being honest about current knowledge without exaggerating, while maintaining confidence in personal capabilities.
Researching the business model, understanding the role, and demonstrating professional readiness.

workplace_qualities.description: Consistently delivering measurable value and building long-term client relationships.
Collaborating internationally and leveraging global insights for solutions.
Valuing diversity and fostering a trusting, open, and inclusive environment.
Maintaining a 'can-do' attitude and supporting team development.
Being ethically unyielding, honest, and accountable for outcomes.
Acting with an owner mentality to build a durable company and improve communities.

values.name: Create the future
values.description: Pursue new ideas and bold goals, and have the courage to try something that has never been done.

values.name: Own the outcome
values.description: Take responsibility for results, act like an owner, and see things through.

values.name: Raise the bar
values.description: Hold yourself and your work to a high standard and keep improving it.

values.name: Be genuine
values.description: Be sincere, honest and inclusive in how you work with others.

interview_expectations.description: Demonstrating the four core values: Create the future, Own the outcome, Raise the bar, and Be genuine.
Anticipating unmet customer needs and focusing on delivering unparalleled value to delight users.
Meeting a high bar for excellence through rigorous problem-solving and a passion for digital experiences.
Being direct about failures or challenges and showing a continuous desire to improve and do better.
Displaying a bias toward action and understanding how individual contributions impact broader company outcomes.

workplace_qualities.description: Relentlessly driving innovation, challenging the status quo, and transforming the industry.
Taking full accountability for both daily tasks and the ultimate business impact of a project.
Continuously evolving, never settling for 'good enough,' and striving to be the best.
Supporting colleagues with honesty, sincerity, and direct communication.
Fostering a diverse, respectful environment where great ideas are welcomed from anywhere.

values.name: Customer Obsession
values.description: Leaders start with the customer and work backwards. They work vigorously to earn and keep customer trust, and although they pay attention to competitors, they obsess over customers.

values.name: Ownership
values.description: Leaders are owners. They think long term, don't sacrifice long-term value for short-term results, act on behalf of the entire company, and never say 'that's not my job'.

values.name: Invent and Simplify
values.description: Leaders expect and require innovation and invention from their teams and always find ways to simplify. They look for new ideas from everywhere and accept being misunderstood for long periods.

values.name: Are Right, A Lot
values.description: Leaders have strong judgment and good instincts. They seek diverse perspectives and work to disconfirm their beliefs.

values.name: Learn and Be Curious
values.description: Leaders are never done learning and always seek to improve themselves. They are curious about new possibilities and act to explore them.

values.name: Hire and Develop the Best
values.description: Leaders raise the performance bar with every hire and promotion, recognise exceptional talent, and take seriously their role in coaching others.

values.name: Insist on the Highest Standards
values.description: Leaders have relentlessly high standards, continually raise the bar, ensure defects are not sent down the line, and fix problems so they stay fixed.

values.name: Think Big
values.description: Thinking small is a self-fulfilling prophecy. Leaders create and communicate a bold direction that inspires results, and look around corners for ways to serve customers.

values.name: Bias for Action
values.description: Speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. Amazon values calculated risk taking.

values.name: Frugality
values.description: Accomplish more with less. Constraints breed resourcefulness, self-sufficiency and invention; there are no extra points for growing headcount, budget or fixed expense.

values.name: Earn Trust
values.description: Leaders listen attentively, speak candidly, treat others respectfully, and are vocally self-critical even when it is awkward or embarrassing.

values.name: Dive Deep
values.description: Leaders operate at all levels, stay connected to the details, audit frequently, and are sceptical when metrics and anecdote differ. No task is beneath them.

values.name: Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit
values.description: Leaders respectfully challenge decisions when they disagree, even when it is uncomfortable, and do not compromise for social cohesion. Once a decision is made, they commit wholly.

values.name: Deliver Results
values.description: Leaders focus on the key inputs for their business and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, they rise to the occasion and never settle.

values.name: Strive to be Earth's Best Employer
values.description: Leaders work to create a safer, more productive, higher performing, more diverse and more just work environment, and lead with empathy.

values.name: Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility
values.description: Amazon is big and impacts the world. Leaders are humble and thoughtful about even the secondary effects of their actions, and leave things better than they found them.

interview_expectations.description: Every answer is heavily evaluated against Amazon's 16 Leadership Principles. Candidates are expected to map their past experiences directly to these principles.
Candidates must structure their answers using the Situation, Task, Action, Result (STAR) method, heavily emphasizing quantifiable metrics and hard data to back up their claims.
Demonstrating a mindset of starting with the customer and working backwards. Interviewers look for candidates who prioritize user needs over technical ego or short-term gains.
Candidates must prove they are better than 50% of the current employees in that specific role, showing potential to elevate the team's overall standards.
Providing concrete examples of taking initiative without being asked, taking calculated risks, and owning the outcome regardless of failure or success.

workplace_qualities.description: Amazon relies on detailed, 6-page written narratives rather than PowerPoint presentations. Employees are expected to communicate complex ideas clearly through writing and dive deep into details.
Employees act on behalf of the entire company, not just their team. They never say 'that's not my job' and avoid sacrificing long-term value for short-term results.
Workers are obligated to respectfully challenge decisions they disagree with, even when doing so is uncomfortable. However, once a decision is made, they must commit wholly to its execution.
A relentless focus on rising to the occasion, hitting deadlines, and delivering the right quality inputs, even when faced with significant setbacks.
Accomplishing more with less. Employees are expected to foster resourcefulness and self-sufficiency without relying on expanding headcount or budget size.
Leaders are expected to require innovation from their teams and always find ways to simplify complex, scalable systems.

interview_expectations.description: Interviewers look for a genuine, deep-seated passion for Apple products, design philosophy, and the ecosystem. Candidates must demonstrate how their work aligns with Apple's mission to enrich lives.
Whether in code, design, or problem-solving, candidates are expected to show a perfectionist mindset. Apple values those who care deeply about the micro-details that impact the final user experience.
Candidates are often tested with vague or highly ambiguous problems. They must demonstrate the ability to ask the right questions, pivot quickly, and create structure out of chaos.

Apple maintains a notoriously high bar for hard skills. Candidates must prove they are subject matter experts in their specific domain, capable of building highly optimized, scalable, and flawless solutions.
Given Apple's culture of secrecy, interviewers evaluate a candidate's professionalism, integrity, and ability to handle confidential information responsibly.

workplace_qualities.description: Apple operates on extreme accountability. Every project or task has a DRI who takes absolute ownership of the outcome, whether it succeeds or fails, without making excuses.
The workplace is heavily compartmentalized. Employees must adhere to strict confidentiality rules, working on a 'need-to-know' basis to protect unreleased products and intellectual property.
Employees are expected to exhibit uncompromising standards for quality. 'Good enough' is never accepted; the focus is always on delivering the absolute best version of a product or feature.
Because Apple seamlessly integrates hardware, software, and services, employees must excel at collaborating across different teams and disciplines without ego.
Every decision made internally must prioritize the end-user. Employees are expected to view their technical or business contributions through the lens of customer empathy and simplicity.
Apple's culture is demanding and fast-paced. Employees are expected to show high dedication, often working rigorously to meet non-negotiable launch deadlines.

values.name: Open company, no bull
values.description: Information is open internally by default, and people are candid and transparent rather than political.

values.name: Build with heart and balance
values.description: Combine passion and urgency with the care to consider options fully: measure twice, cut once.

values.name: Don't mess with the customer
values.description: Customers are the lifeblood of the company; their perspective comes first in every decision.

values.name: Play, as a team
values.description: Work hard together without taking yourselves too seriously, and put the team ahead of individual credit.

values.name: Be the change you seek
values.description: Have the courage and resourcefulness to spark change and make the products, people and place better.

interview_expectations.description: Atlassian runs a dedicated values interview for every candidate, scored against its five company values, with behavioural questions about real situations.
Interviewers look for people who play as a team, share credit, and work well across functions and time zones in a largely distributed company.
Candidates should show they think about how their work affects the customer, and make decisions from the customer's point of view.
Coding rounds emphasise clean, working, well-tested code and practical problem solving over puzzle tricks.
Being honest about mistakes and what you don't know, and giving and receiving feedback constructively.

workplace_qualities.description: Information is shared openly internally, and teams work transparently.
A distributed-first way of working that relies on clear written communication and async collaboration.
Decisions start with what the customer needs.
Passion and urgency are balanced with care and sustainable pace.
Everyone is responsible for making products, processes and teams better.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates are expected to demonstrate strong proficiency in data structures, algorithms, and system design, often with a focus on optimizing for time and space complexity in low-latency environments.
Interviewers look for candidates who treat technical rounds as a pair-programming session, asking clarifying questions, communicating their thought process, and taking hints constructively.
Candidates must clearly explain the 'why' behind their technical decisions, weighing the pros and cons of different approaches and data structures.
While prior finance knowledge is not strictly required, candidates should show a genuine curiosity about real-time data, financial markets, and the impact of information at scale.
The ability to quickly pivot or optimize a naive solution on the fly when the interviewer introduces new constraints or scales up the problem.

workplace_qualities.description: Bloomberg operates in a highly transparent, open-office environment designed to foster high-bandwidth communication, quick decision-making, and spontaneous teamwork.
Employees must prioritize system stability and speed. The Bloomberg Terminal is mission-critical for global finance, meaning software failures are not an option.

A strong commitment to giving back is deeply ingrained in the culture, with a large majority of the company's profits funding Bloomberg Philanthropies. Employees are encouraged to participate in volunteer programs.
Workers are expected to thrive in a fast-paced environment, deploying code frequently and iterating quickly to meet the rapidly changing demands of the market.
Engineers and professionals are expected to take full responsibility for their products, managing the entire lifecycle from initial design and development to production monitoring and maintenance.
Valuing diverse perspectives and inclusive practices to effectively build products and provide services for a highly diverse, global client base.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates are expected to display a highly entrepreneurial mindset. Interviewers look for ambition, resilience, and a hunger to innovate without settling for the status quo.
Aligning with their 'Seek Truth and Pragmatic' value, candidates must demonstrate how they use objective data and metrics to guide their decisions, rather than relying on gut feelings.
For technical roles, candidates face a very high bar for coding and system design. They must prove their ability to build and optimize systems capable of handling massive, global user traffic.
Interviewers test for agility. Candidates must show they can thrive in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment where ambiguity is common and pivoting is frequently required.
Candidates should communicate their ideas concisely and directly, proving they can engage in the flat, open dialogue that ByteDance values.

workplace_qualities.description: Employees are expected to avoid complacency, continuously push boundaries, and approach their work with the same urgency and innovation as a startup, regardless of the company's size.
The culture heavily relies on objectivity. Workers must focus on uncovering the root cause of problems, relying on A/B testing and data analytics, and executing practical solutions.
ByteDance promotes a flat organizational culture where title matters less than the idea. Employees are expected to speak their minds, give direct feedback, and avoid corporate bureaucracy.
Workers are challenged to set extremely ambitious goals, refuse mediocrity, and constantly raise the bar for themselves and their teams to achieve maximum impact.
Employees are encouraged to take big, calculated risks while remaining grounded in reality and taking ownership of the gritty, hands-on work required to bring big ideas to life.
Operating globally, employees must excel at collaborating across different cultures, time zones, and backgrounds to build products that appeal to a diverse worldwide audience.

values.name: Customer obsessed
values.description: The customer is at the centre of everything; what is best for the customer is best for Databricks.

values.name: Raise the bar
values.description: Every day is an opportunity to do even better, as individuals and as a company.

values.name: Truth seeking
values.description: Make decisions based on data, and change your mind as the data changes.

values.name: First principles
values.description: Reason from fundamentals rather than analogy or convention to drive innovation.

values.name: Bias for action
values.description: Move with urgency and prefer doing and learning over lengthy deliberation.

values.name: Company first
values.description: Put the success of the company ahead of the interests of any one team or individual.

interview_expectations.description: Interviewers expect candidates to break down complex problems into their fundamental truths rather than relying on analogies or 'how it's always been done.' Candidates must demonstrate logical, from-scratch reasoning.

For technical roles, there is a rigorous bar for understanding distributed systems, big data architecture, and cloud computing. Candidates must prove they can design and optimize systems for massive scale.
Candidates must show a track record of letting data guide their decisions. Interviewers look for individuals who naturally back up their claims, architectures, and strategies with empirical metrics.
Candidates need to demonstrate a deep understanding of user pain points. Answers should highlight how past projects directly simplified workflows or solved critical problems for end-users.
Interviewers assess cultural fit by looking for a 'Teamwork makes the dream work' mentality. Candidates must show they can collaborate cross-functionally and accept constructive feedback gracefully.

workplace_qualities.description: The customer is at the centre of everything; what is best for the customer is best for Databricks.
Every day is an opportunity to do even better, as individuals and as a company.
Make decisions based on data, and change your mind as the data changes.
Reason from fundamentals rather than analogy or convention to drive innovation.
Move with urgency and prefer doing and learning over lengthy deliberation.
Put the success of the company ahead of the interests of any one team or individual.

values.name: Lead the way
values.description: Take the lead in shaping the profession, the market and society, and have the courage to act.

values.name: Serve with integrity
values.description: Hold to the highest ethical and professional standards and earn trust through what you do.

values.name: Take care of each other
values.description: Look out for colleagues' wellbeing and help each other grow.

values.name: Foster inclusion
values.description: Create an environment where everyone feels they belong and can contribute.

values.name: Collaborate for measurable impact
values.description: Work across teams and with clients to deliver results that make a measurable difference.

interview_expectations.description: Especially for consulting and advisory roles, candidates must excel in case interviews by structuring ambiguous problems, applying strong business acumen, and doing quick mental math.
Interviewers assess behavioral alignment with Deloitte's core values: Lead the way, Serve with integrity, Take care of each other, Foster inclusion, and Collaborate for measurable impact.
Candidates must demonstrate executive presence, active listening, and the ability to articulate complex solutions clearly and persuasively, mimicking how they would speak to a C-suite client.
Interviewers look for individuals who can seamlessly pivot between different industries, technologies, and team structures, given the fast-paced nature of professional services.
Candidates need to provide concrete examples of leading initiatives while also functioning as a highly cooperative team player in matrixed environments.

workplace_qualities.description: Employees are held to the absolute highest ethical standards. This includes strict adherence to independence rules, client confidentiality, and unbiased professional judgment.
Workers are expected to break down silos, leverage Deloitte's massive global network of subject matter experts, and deliver tangible, transformative value to clients.
The culture heavily emphasizes mentorship, coaching, and well-being. Professionals are expected to support their peers' career development and prioritize a healthy team dynamic.
Deloitte demands a workplace where diversity is celebrated. Employees must act as allies, actively include diverse perspectives, and cultivate psychological safety.
Employees are encouraged to show courage, challenge the status quo, and act as innovators and thought leaders (building 'eminence') in their respective practice areas.
In a firm built on knowledge, employees are expected to take ownership of their continuous education, obtaining industry certifications and staying ahead of market trends.

values.name: Audacity
values.description: Take bold bets and change the paradigm rather than settle for incremental improvement.

values.name: Bias for Action
values.description: Have a sense of urgency to solve problems and put good ideas into action.

values.name: Customer First
values.description: Look at the world from the customer's point of view and keep them at the heart of every decision.

values.name: Integrity
values.description: Always do the right thing and stay committed to customers and stakeholders.

values.name: Inclusion
values.description: Celebrate diversity of thought, style and background, and make everyone feel they belong.

interview_expectations.description: Interviewers strongly evaluate candidates against Flipkart’s five core values: Audacity, Bias for Action, Customer-First, Integrity, and Inclusion. Candidates should prepare examples that showcase these traits.
Candidates must demonstrate the ability to think critically and solve complex problems within a commerce context. This involves connecting user needs, supply chain logistics, and business impact.

Depending on the role, candidates face rigorous functional assessments (e.g., Data Structures, Algorithms, and scalable System Design for engineers; product sense, metrics, and prioritization for PMs).
Interviewers look for candidates who question the status quo, embrace unconventional ways of thinking, and don't blindly accept things just because 'they were done that way before.'
The ability to handle conflicting priorities, pivot during sudden changes in project requirements, and manage high-pressure situations with a positive, collaborative mindset.

workplace_qualities.description: Take bold bets and change the paradigm rather than settle for incremental improvement.
Have a sense of urgency to solve problems and put good ideas into action.
Look at the world from the customer's point of view and keep them at the heart of every decision.
Always do the right thing and stay committed to customers and stakeholders.
Celebrate diversity of thought, style and background, and make everyone feel they belong.

values.name: Partnership
values.description: Teamwork and collaboration across the firm; success is shared and no one person is bigger than the firm.

values.name: Client Service
values.description: Clients' interests always come first; the firm succeeds only when its clients succeed.

values.name: Integrity
values.description: Integrity and honesty are at the heart of the business, and reputation is the firm's most important asset.

values.name: Excellence
values.description: Hold yourself to the highest standards and never settle for anything less than the best.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates are expected to be familiar with Goldman Sachs' 14 Business Principles and must demonstrate how their past experiences and personal values align with these core tenets.

Whether interviewing for engineering, quantitative (strats), or investment banking roles, candidates must display sharp analytical skills, mental math proficiency, and an understanding of how their work impacts broader financial markets.

The firm operates in a high-stakes, zero-error environment. Interviewers look for extreme precision in how candidates present themselves, structure their resumes, and solve technical or case problems.
Goldman Sachs has a highly collaborative culture. Candidates must use the STAR method to show they can work effectively in teams, share credit, and navigate differing opinions without ego.
Interviewers test for grit and the ability to thrive under pressure. Candidates must show they can handle intense, fast-paced environments and steep learning curves.

workplace_qualities.description: This is the firm's first Business Principle. Employees are expected to prioritize the client's long-term success above short-term firm gains or individual recognition.
Employees operate in a highly regulated industry and must adhere strictly to compliance, confidentiality, and ethical standards. Honesty and character are considered non-negotiable.
Workers must maintain an unrelenting focus on quality. 'Good enough' is unacceptable; employees are expected to deliver world-class execution in every task, no matter how small.

The firm heavily relies on an apprenticeship model. Professionals are expected to proactively seek mentorship from senior leaders while simultaneously investing time in training and developing junior talent.
Decisions at Goldman Sachs are rarely made in silos. Employees must excel at cross-divisional networking, building consensus among stakeholders, and working seamlessly across global offices.
The workplace is highly competitive but fair. Advancement depends entirely on performance, impact, and adherence to the firm's cultural values, encouraging a highly self-driven workforce.

interview_expectations.description: Interviewers assess how candidates learn, solve complex problems, and navigate ambiguous situations. The focus is on the thought process and adaptability rather than just getting the 'right' answer.
Candidates must demonstrate deep, functional expertise for the specific role. For software engineers, this means rigorous data structures, algorithms, and scalable system design.
Google looks for candidates who know when to step up and lead a team through a problem, and equally importantly, when to step back and let others take the reins.
A cultural assessment looking for traits like intellectual humility, comfort with ambiguity, a bias to action, collaborative nature, and a strong inner drive to do the right thing.
The ability to break down massive, open-ended questions into structured, manageable components and communicate those steps clearly to the interviewer.

workplace_qualities.description: Following the core philosophy, 'Focus on the user and all else will follow,' employees are expected to prioritize user experience and needs above internal goals or short-term monetization.
Employees are encouraged to think about how to make something ten times better rather than just 10% better, fostering a culture of radical innovation and scalable solutions.
Google highly values teams where members feel safe to take risks and voice opinions without fear of judgment, fostering inclusive collaboration and 'blameless post-mortems' when things fail.
The workplace relies heavily on data and A/B testing to settle debates. Employees must use empirical evidence to back up their ideas, product changes, and strategies.
Information is widely shared across the company to spark innovation. Employees are expected to be transparent with their projects, share code, and contribute to internal knowledge bases.
A commitment to acting with integrity, evaluating the ethical implications of technology, and maintaining trust with users, partners, and the broader global community.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates must demonstrate a deep understanding of the end-user—primarily retail investors in India. Interviewers look for the ability to simplify complex financial concepts into intuitive user experiences.
For engineering roles, candidates are heavily tested on their ability to design highly scalable, concurrent systems capable of handling massive traffic spikes during stock market hours.
The fintech space is fast-paced and heavily regulated. Interviewers expect candidates to show how they can navigate ambiguous problems, pivot quickly, and find compliant yet innovative solutions.

interview_expectations.quality: Bias for Action and Startup Mindset
interview_expectations.description: Candidates should provide examples of taking initiative, moving fast, and getting things done without waiting for perfect conditions or extensive hand-holding.
Reflecting the company's core ethos, candidates are expected to be upfront about what they know and what they don't, showing a willingness to learn rather than bluffing through answers.

workplace_qualities.description: Every decision made at Groww starts with the customer. Employees are expected to prioritize the financial safety, education, and user experience of retail investors above all else.
The company's mission is to make investing accessible. Workers must continually strive to eliminate complexity from products, codebases, and internal processes, championing a frictionless experience.
Just as Groww promises no hidden charges to its users, employees are expected to maintain open, honest, and direct communication across all levels of the organization.
Employees are empowered to act like owners. This means taking full end-to-end responsibility for projects, owning the failures just as much as the successes, and driving initiatives to completion.
The Indian financial market and regulatory landscape change rapidly. Workers must be highly adaptable, capable of shipping features quickly, and iterating based on real-time feedback.
Employees are expected to operate efficiently, finding smart, scalable ways to solve problems while keeping unit economics and sustainable growth in mind.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates must strongly align with the bank's core philosophy that 'Ethics are always above business,' demonstrating high integrity, transparency, and moral standards during behavioral rounds.
Interviewers look for a genuine focus on customer delight, assessing the candidate's ability to prioritize user needs, resolve pain points, and build long-term trust in financial services.
Candidates should exhibit a 'Digital First' mindset. Whether in tech or business roles, they must show readiness to leverage modern digital solutions to simplify and scale banking operations.

Candidates should display a genuine interest in social impact and financial inclusion, aligning with the bank's explicit mission to be a 'Force for Social Good' and touch millions of lives positively.
Candidates must communicate with empathy and collaboration, proving they can thrive in a workplace culture that heavily emphasizes mutual respect, open dialogue, and a lack of hierarchical ego.

workplace_qualities.description: Employees are expected to uphold uncompromising ethical practices and regulatory compliance in all dealings, ensuring that doing the right thing always supersedes short-term profits.
Workers are empowered to continuously innovate and design seamless, customer-centric products that redefine the banking experience for both urban and underserved rural populations.
Employees are encouraged to participate in 'FIRST IMPACT' (the bank's CSR initiative) and contribute to sustainable development, education, sanitation, and community-building.

The culture promotes boundary-less working. Employees are expected to take ownership of their career paths and leverage internal AI-driven platforms (like iTalent) for continuous professional development.
Through initiatives like the 'iBelong' Charter, employees must foster an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are recognized as a core strength that powers agility.
Employees are encouraged to pursue personal interests and maintain a healthy work-life balance, supported by the bank's 'Tann-Mann-Dhan' (Body-Mind-Wealth) wellness philosophy.

values.name: Client Value
values.description: Surpass client expectations consistently by delivering predictable, high-quality results.

values.name: Leadership by Example
values.description: Set standards for the industry and for yourself, and lead through your own actions.

values.name: Integrity and Transparency
values.description: Be ethical, sincere and open in all dealings.

values.name: Fairness
values.description: Be objective and transaction-oriented, and earn trust and respect through fair treatment.

values.name: Excellence
values.description: Strive relentlessly to improve yourself, your team, your services and your products.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates are assessed on their alignment with Infosys's core values: Client value, Leadership by example, Integrity and transparency, Fairness, and Excellence.
Interviewers test fundamental problem-solving abilities, logical reasoning, data structures, and core software engineering concepts, reflecting the structured training approach of the company.
Candidates must show an understanding of how to translate business requirements into efficient technical solutions while keeping the global enterprise client's goals front and center.
Given the rapid shifts in enterprise tech (Cloud, AI, Automation), candidates must display a strong hunger for continuous upskilling and learning agility.
Professionalism, clear articulation of thoughts, and active listening are heavily evaluated, especially for client-facing and global delivery roles.

workplace_qualities.description: Employees are expected to consistently deliver predictable, high-quality results that create long-term value for global clients across diverse industries.
Uncompromising commitment to ethical business practices, honesty, and corporate governance in all internal and external operations.
Every employee is encouraged to take ownership of their work, set high performance standards, and lead initiatives proactively without waiting for top-down direction.
Employees are expected to continuously upgrade their skills using platforms like Infosys Springboard, staying ahead of digital transformation trends such as AI and cloud computing.
Working across multi-cultural global teams requires deep respect for diversity, active collaboration, and an inclusive mindset.
Operating with mutual respect, meritocracy, and fairness in team dynamics, appraisals, and career growth trajectories.

values.name: Members first
values.description: Every decision starts with what is best for LinkedIn's members.

values.name: Relationships matter
values.description: Build strong, lasting relationships with colleagues, customers and members.

values.name: Be open, honest and constructive
values.description: Give and receive candid feedback in a way that helps people improve.

values.name: Demand excellence
values.description: Hold yourself and others to a high bar and keep raising it.

values.name: Take intelligent risks
values.description: Make bold, informed bets, and learn from the ones that fail.

values.name: Act like an owner
values.description: Take responsibility for outcomes beyond your immediate role.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates are explicitly evaluated against LinkedIn's core cultural values (Transformation, Integrity, Collaboration, Humor, and Results), often through dedicated behavioral rounds.
Interviewers test whether candidates naturally prioritize the professional community and user experience over short-term monetization or insular metrics, aligning with the platform's vision.

For engineering tracks, candidates face deep-dive technical rounds focusing on large-scale distributed systems, graph data processing, and resilient architecture capable of serving hundreds of millions of professionals.
Candidates must demonstrate how they partner effectively with product management, design, data science, and operations teams to bring complex ideas to life.
The ability to articulate thoughts clearly, receive constructive feedback gracefully during technical sessions, and engage in respectful debate is heavily emphasized.

workplace_qualities.description: Employees are encouraged to constantly evolve—transforming themselves, their products, and the global professional landscape through bold ideas and continuous innovation.
Maintaining an environment of absolute trust, protecting member data privacy, and acting ethically in every decision, ensuring the platform remains a safe professional haven.
Fostering a 'one team' mentality where diverse perspectives are actively welcomed, psychological safety is prioritized, and collective success outweighs individual ego.
A core cultural pillar that encourages employees not to take themselves too seriously, maintaining a lighthearted, joyful, and balanced work environment.
While culture and people come first, employees are expected to exhibit a strong bias for impact, executing efficiently and delivering high-quality, measurable outcomes.
Embracing a flexible, employee-centric work model that supports personal well-being, continuous learning days (InDays), and a healthy integration of life and career.

interview_expectations.description: Candidates are expected to demonstrate strong foundational knowledge in their domain (software engineering, cloud, data, etc.) and a logical approach to solving complex, real-world technical problems.
Interviewers evaluate the candidate's ability to understand the business context behind the technology, focusing on how their technical solutions will deliver tangible value to the client.
Given the fast-paced nature of IT consulting, candidates must show a high aptitude for continuous learning and a willingness to quickly adapt to new tools, technologies, and project environments.

Clear articulation of thoughts is crucial. Candidates are assessed on their ability to explain complex technical concepts in a simple, understandable manner, which is essential for client-facing roles.
Emphasis is placed on teamwork, ethical grounding, and alignment with the overarching values of the Larsen & Toubro (L&T) group, including reliability and professionalism.

workplace_qualities.description: Employees are expected to act as true partners to their clients, actively listening, anticipating needs, and consistently delivering high-quality digital solutions that drive business growth.
A strong culture of learning where employees are encouraged and supported to pursue certifications, master cutting-edge technologies, and bring innovative ideas to the table.
The ability to operate in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, delivering projects with speed, precision, and a strong bias for action without compromising on quality.
Working seamlessly across global geographies and diverse teams, sharing knowledge, and fostering an inclusive environment where collective goals supersede individual achievements.

workplace_qualities.description: A foundational cultural pillar prioritizing absolute integrity, ethical decision-making, and regulatory compliance, ensuring the company operates responsibly in every market.
Maintaining a strong bias for action and an entrepreneurial hustle. Employees are encouraged to take extreme ownership of their domains and execute with speed, grit, and determination.

Fostering a deeply collaborative environment that actively breaks down departmental silos. Employees are expected to prioritize the overarching success of the company (Rides, Eats, Freight) over individual or team metrics.
Keeping deep empathy for the users and earners at the core of every decision, ensuring that the technology built genuinely improves the daily lives and economic opportunities of people globally.
An uncompromising, non-negotiable commitment to ensuring both the physical and digital safety of everyone who interacts with the platform, from riders and drivers to internal data systems.

workplace_qualities.quality: See the Forest and the Trees
workplace_qualities.description: The ability to operate at multiple altitudes—employees must understand the high-level strategic vision of the company while meticulously managing the granular, operational details required to execute it.

values.name: Lead by example
values.description: Model the behaviour you expect, with integrity and accountability.

values.name: Communicate openly
values.description: Share information transparently and listen to others.

values.name: Act decisively
values.description: Make timely decisions and move with urgency.

values.name: Excel with partners
values.description: Collaborate closely with clients and partners to deliver value.

values.name: Enable and inspire
values.description: Develop people and help them do their best work.

interview_expectations.description: For technical roles, candidates are rigorously evaluated on their ability to design highly available, fault-tolerant distributed systems capable of processing thousands of transactions per second (TPS) with zero downtime and absolute security.

Interviewers look for a structured approach to problem-solving, focusing on optimal data structures, clean code, and edge-case handling to ensure low-latency and high-throughput in critical financial systems.
Given the heavily regulated global payments landscape, candidates must demonstrate an understanding of data privacy, fraud prevention, and the importance of adhering to strict compliance standards.
Evaluators assess whether candidates understand the broader financial ecosystem, focusing on how their solutions will empower financial institutions, merchants, and everyday consumers.

The ability to articulate complex technical architectures or business tradeoffs clearly, take constructive feedback, and demonstrate an aptitude for working seamlessly in a heavily matrixed, global team.

workplace_qualities.description: Employees are expected to act with uncompromising integrity, model inclusive behaviors, and maintain the highest ethical standards, ensuring trust remains the bedrock of the brand.

A cultural emphasis on radical transparency and active listening. Employees must break down silos, share information freely, and engage in respectful, open dialogue across all levels of the organization.
Fostering a strong bias for action. Employees are encouraged to make informed, data-driven decisions swiftly and execute efficiently to keep pace with the rapidly evolving fintech landscape.

A relentless focus on co-creation and mutual success. Teams are expected to build deep, collaborative relationships with banks, fintechs, and merchants to drive value across the entire global payments network.
Leaders and peers are expected to empower one another, champion continuous learning, and foster an environment where diverse perspectives and innovative ideas are actively celebrated.
The non-negotiable core of Visa's operations. Every employee is responsible for upholding the safety, security, and flawlessly reliable uptime of the global financial infrastructure.

interview_expectations.description: For technical roles, candidates are evaluated on designing real-time, highly concurrent systems capable of instant inventory synchronization across dark stores and sub-minute dispatch routing.
Given its hyper-growth startup environment, interviewers heavily screen for candidates who can execute rapidly with limited resources, showing a strong hustle and hands-on approach.
Candidates must demonstrate the ability to break down complex quick-commerce challenges—from last-mile logistics to supply chain forecasting—without relying on traditional e-commerce playbooks.
Evaluators expect candidates to be extremely data-driven, using granular analytics to optimize processes, improve unit economics, and literally shave seconds off fulfillment times.
The ability to navigate extreme ambiguity, pivot quickly as business priorities shift, and maintain composure in a fiercely competitive and fast-paced market.

workplace_qualities.description: The foundational DNA of the company. This applies not just to the 10-minute delivery promise, but to how teams operate, iterate on products, and launch new initiatives.
Employees are expected to act with a founder's mentality, taking complete end-to-end accountability for their tasks, outcomes, and the overall success of their specific domains.
A relentless focus on driving profitability and perfect unit economics through ruthless efficiency, minimizing waste across the supply chain and dark store operations.
Ensuring that the pursuit of speed never compromises the quality of the products delivered or the trust of the consumer, prioritizing a seamless user experience.
A culture that rejects assumptions in favor of hard numbers. Every operational tweak and product feature is fiercely debated and validated using real-time data.
Encouraging employees to challenge legacy retail and traditional e-commerce models, continuously pioneering new ways to redefine convenience for the modern consumer.

interview_expectations.description: Unlike many tech giants, Zoho emphasizes raw logical aptitude over academic pedigree. Initial rounds heavily focus on deep fundamentals in C, C++, or Java, memory management, and foundational problem-solving.

Candidates are frequently tested on their ability to design and build functional modules or complex mini-applications from scratch in a restricted environment, prioritizing hands-on coding skills over theoretical puzzles.

Interviewers look for developers who can solve complex problems without heavily relying on third-party frameworks or external libraries, aligning with Zoho's philosophy of building software from the ground up.
Evaluators seek low-ego, highly curious individuals who demonstrate a strong willingness to learn and adapt, deeply reflecting the inclusive ethos of the Zoho Schools of Learning.

Because of its unique culture, interviewers try to gauge a candidate's desire for stability and long-term career growth, favoring those who want to build lasting products rather than frequently job-hop.

workplace_qualities.description: A pioneering commitment to decentralizing technology. Zoho heavily invests in rural and non-urban offices, aiming to bring high-tech jobs and economic upliftment directly to local communities.

Fiercely proud of being privately held, profitable, and debt-free. Employees operate without the pressure of venture capital or quarterly public market expectations, allowing for patient, long-term innovation.

A culture obsessed with building everything in-house. From underlying databases and server infrastructure to the entire SaaS suite, Zoho encourages deep engineering to maintain absolute control over its tech stack.

Fostering a deeply supportive, family-like environment with an intense focus on employee well-being, organic career growth, and mutual loyalty, resulting in some of the lowest attrition rates in the industry.

An egalitarian, meritocratic workplace that actively champions raw talent, often hiring and heavily investing in individuals without formal college degrees through its internal, tuition-free educational programs.
A focus on operational frugality and customer value. The company channels its resources primarily into engineering and product development rather than extravagant marketing or sales spend.

interview_expectations.quality: Real-Time System Design and High Availability
interview_expectations.description: For engineering roles, candidates are rigorously tested on their ability to architect scalable, low-latency distributed systems that handle geospatial routing and massive, unpredictable traffic spikes (e.g., during festivals or sports finals).
Interviewers evaluate whether candidates can strip away industry jargon and tackle complex logistics, quick-commerce, and marketplace challenges using fundamental, logical reasoning.
Candidates must demonstrate a deep understanding of Zomato's three-sided ecosystem, balancing the competing priorities of end consumers, restaurant/merchant partners, and delivery executives.

Evaluators look for self-starters who operate with a strong bias for action. Candidates must showcase past experiences where they navigated extreme ambiguity and delivered results with minimal supervision.
Candidates are expected to rely on hard metrics to justify their decisions, demonstrating how data analytics can optimize delivery ETAs, personalize user feeds, and improve overall unit economics.

workplace_qualities.description: A core cultural pillar where employees are expected to act as owners of the business, taking bold, calculated risks, and accepting complete end-to-end accountability for their successes and failures.
The ultimate true north for the company. Every new feature, UI tweak, and operational pivot is reverse-engineered from the goal of maximizing user convenience, delight, and trust.
A workplace that thrives on brutal honesty and open communication. Employees are encouraged to debate fiercely, give and receive direct feedback, and prioritize the best idea over hierarchy.
Operating in a hyper-competitive landscape, teams are pushed to execute with extreme urgency, ship MVPs quickly, and iterate relentlessly based on real-world market feedback.

A strong emphasis on doing more with less. Employees are expected to optimize resources rigorously to drive operational efficiency and maintain sustainable profitability across all business verticals.
A relentless drive to evolve beyond core food delivery, actively pioneering and integrating new verticals such as quick commerce (Blinkit), dining out, B2B supplies (Hyperpure), and live events.
